answer: Give each newcomer a one-shot computational landmark: it must first occupy a unique knoll in a public hash space that no other key already claims. From there it climbs a terrace of timed, peer-replayable chores whose outputs hash together into a lineage. The ledger treats the completed lineage as an anchor for voting weight and slashes any later key that reuses a prior output. A sybil farm cannot fork that lineage without repeating the exclusive work, so extra identities stall rather than multiply ballots.
